cards.title: Sensitivity Analysis and Parameter Uncertainty
cards.claim: Sensitivity analysis is required to understand how changes in key input parameters (due to uncertainty or variability) influence model output. It should be performed for parameters considered key to the model or uncertain (e.g., those with literature variability, optimized during building, or difficult to measure). A 'worst-case' approach is recommended (e.g., 10-fold for CYP enzymes, 30-fold for transporters). Global or joint sensitivity analyses may be used to assess correlated parameters.
conditions: Must be performed during both model development and application.
Ranges for sensitivity analysis must be pre-specified and justified based on scientific rationale or published data.
Applicable to both system-dependent and drug-dependent parameters.
required_inputs: Methodology for global or joint sensitivity analysis if parameters are correlated.
limitations: Does not specify the exact statistical method for sensitivity analysis beyond 'systematic investigation'.
Specific fold-change examples (10-fold/30-fold) are illustrative, not universal mandates for all parameters.
cards.downstream_use: Informs the uncertainty analysis in human simulation scenarios. Helps identify which parameters drive exposure variability and require precise measurement or justification.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
